_comment: Annotated example. Copy this alongside a real character sheet's frames, rename to registration.json, and fill in real values. See tools/check_registration.py's docstring for the full schema.
_actor_type_comment: 'walk-plane' for a freely-walking actor, 'furniture-anchored' for a fixed/windowed actor (behind a counter, desk, gate, etc).
_canvas_comment: Every frame file in this sheet must be exactly this pixel size. A mismatch is a hard fail.
_tolerance_comment: How many pixels of anchor drift between frames is tolerated before the frames check fails. Keep this small — it exists to catch registration mistakes, not to permit them.

frames._anchor_comment: The confirmed contact point for THIS frame: foot-ground contact for a walk-plane actor, or the counter/desk-contact line's center point for a furniture-anchored actor. This is authored/confirmed by a human, never inferred from pixel content.
frames._role_comment: Free-text label for what this frame is in the walk-cycle contract (see ANIMATION_BIBLE.md) — not read by the tool, but keeps the sheet self-documenting.

frames._canonical_comment: Exactly one frame per sheet should be marked canonical:true — the character's neutral/idle standing pose. This is the frame cast-scale measures from.
frames._scale_reference_comment: Only required on the canonical frame. A second landmark point, by convention the character's head-top in that pose. The vertical distance between 'anchor' and 'scale_reference' on the canonical frame is this character's measured standing height, in this sheet's own source pixels — that measurement is what cast-scale compares across the whole roster.
